newsitem.title: ITALY: Dini wants Europe enshrined in Italy constitution.
newsitem.headline: Dini wants Europe enshrined in Italy constitution.

text.p: Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini proposed on Monday that Italy's constitution should contain a commitment to European integration and the budgetary rigour required for membership of the planned single currency.

Dini made his proposal in a speech to a seminar on reform of the Italian state, which is the focus of a special bicameral commission of parliament that has until June to propose changes to the 1948 constitution.

He said a new constitution should enshrine the principle of European citizenship, the primacy of European Union law over national legislation and a duty to make Italian economic and monetary policy conform to EU requirements.
"Ours will be the first constitution to be rewritten...in the light of the high degree of integration that has already been reached in Europe," Dini said.
"The results of the bicameral commission...must reflect our existence in Europe," he said.

Italy was a founder member of the original European Economic Community (EEC), created under the 1957 Treaty of Rome. Its 40th anniversary will be marked in the Italian capital next week with a meeting of EU foreign ministers and the European Commission.

The country, however, is now struggling to meet the strict budget deficit and debt criteria required by the EU's Maastricht Treaty for founder membership from January 1999 of Europe's new single currency under planned economic and monetary union (EMU).
Dini, a former central banker, said constitutional norms were needed "to make the improvement of public accounts lasting and stable".
Italy's constitution is regarded across the political spectrum as incapable of ensuring efficient and stable government and streamlined law-making by parliament.
